title: Sleeping under a treated net
body: Sleep under an insecticide-treated net every night to prevent malaria, especially children and pregnant women.
author: A. Bello

title: malaria prevention
body: Use treated nets, clear stagnant water, and see a clinic early if you have fever.

title: CLEARING STAGNANT WATER
body: Empty containers and clear gutters so mosquitoes cannot breed near your home.
author: A. Bello

title: Antenatal visits
body: Attend antenatal check-ups at least four times during pregnancy to keep mother and baby healthy.
author: N. Okoro

title: Antenatal care
body: Pregnant women should visit a clinic at least four times for check-ups.
author: N. Okoro

title: Eating well on a budget
body: Combine beans, vegetables, and grains for a balanced meal without spending much.
Eat green leafy vegetables and beans to prevent anaemia.
author: F. Yusuf

title: Wash your hands
body: Wash your hands with soap and clean water before eating and after using the toilet.

title: Handwashing
body: Washing hands with soap and water before meals and after the toilet stops many infections.

title: Safe drinking water
body: Boil or treat water before drinking if you are not sure it is clean.
author: I. Musa

title: Typhoid and clean water
body: Typhoid spreads through dirty water and food. Drink safe water and wash food well.
author: I. Musa

title: First aid for burns
summary: What to do for a minor burn
body: Cool a minor burn under running water for about twenty minutes. Do not apply oil or toothpaste.
author: Dr. Ade

title: Choking help
body: For a choking adult, give firm back blows between the shoulder blades and call for help.
author: Dr. Ade

title: Vaccines for children
body: Take your child for all routine vaccines on time to protect against serious diseases.

title: Immunization schedule
body: Follow the national immunization schedule from birth. Free at most public clinics.

title: Family planning options
body: Talk to a health worker about safe options for spacing your children.
author: G. Eze

title: Fever in children
body: If a child has fever with fits, fast breathing or cannot drink, go to a clinic immediately.

title: Breastfeeding basics
body: Start breastfeeding within the first hour of birth and feed only breast milk for six months.
author: N. Okoro

title: DIARRHOEA AND ORS
body: Give oral rehydration solution (ORS) and continue feeding a child with diarrhoea. Seek help if it does not stop.

title: Malaria in pregnancy
body: Pregnant women should sleep under a treated net and take the preventive medicine a clinic gives them.
author: N. Okoro

title: Healthy snacks for children
body: Offer fruit, groundnuts or boiled eggs instead of sweets and soft drinks.
author: F. Yusuf

title: Clean cooking & smoke
body: Cook in a well-ventilated place to reduce smoke that can harm the lungs.

title: First aid kit at home
body: Keep plasters, clean gauze, antiseptic and ORS at home.
author: Dr. Ade

title: washing hands
body: Wash hands with soap. Especially before eating and after the toilet.
